segments.text: Yes. All right. We'll wait on the queue and we'll begin with our admin session.
All right. Good morning, everyone. Welcome to the commission this morning.
This is Tuesday, October the 6th, 2026. The administrative session of the Georgia Public
Service Commission, turning our attention first to the utility division consent agenda.
Any commissioner, like any item on the consent agenda held or moved to the regular agenda.
Hearing of no such request, all in favor of approving the items on the consent agenda say aye.
Aye.
Aye.
Aye.
Any opposed? All right. Consent agenda passes unanimously with
commissioners Wise, McDonald, Shaw, and Hubbard voting in the affirmative.
All right. We'll move on to the regular agenda.
We'll start with item R1. Morning, Tanika.
Good morning, Tanika Starks. Item R1 is docket number 44669, telecommunication relay service
generic docket, hearing aid distribution program provider, consideration of staff's request for
the commission approval to issue an RFP for hearing aid provider. As discussed in last
telecom committee meeting, staff recommends the following dates for the RFP, which is
listed in your backup. Any questions on R1? Well, thank you staff, Tanika and your staff
for everything you're doing to move forward with this RFP. A lot of folks out there,
as you know, don't understand anything about this program and how the Public Service Commission
is attached to this and has been for a long time. So thank you for what y'all do.
And I think this is a good move to look at this program like you're doing. And I know it's a lot
of work, but thank you for doing it. All right. You've heard staff's recommendation on R1. Any
questions? All right. All in favor of approving staff recommendation on item R1, say aye.
Aye.
Aye.
Aye.
Any opposed? R1 passes unanimously. All right. Moving on to R2. Morning.
Good morning, Commissioners. My name is Arne Parekh. Item R2 is Docket 44280, Georgia Power's
Request for Approval of Nuclear Upgrades, tariff.
Anyone is a voluntary program for large load customers to subscribe to zero emission credits
from additional nuclear generation. Customers pay an upfront contribution and monthly charges
for environmental attributes only. Subscription revenues help offset
upgrade costs and reduce pressure on base rates for all customers.
Staff finds the tariff reasonable, protective of non-participants and in the public interest
and recommends approval contingent on the hatch unit 1 and 2 upgrades in Docket 56002 and 56003.
Thank you.
How much power? How much new power?
Yeah, I might be right.
It'll be.
So the hatch units are 49 megawatts of additional power. And then there's also the Vogel units that
were previously approved. I forget the number on that. About 50 megawatts.
So around 100 megawatts.
Yes. Yeah.
Of carbon free energy paid for by somebody else.
So for the most part. So with incremental costs covered by somebody else.
Why don't you bring us some more of those deals?
We'd love to.
That's tongue in cheek. That's okay.
I know there was a lot there. There may be some questions. We had some great questions
last week in committee and and I just appreciate I know staff and Mr.
Trokey had responded with some backup soon after our committees last week.
That was my opinion very, very helpful. So I appreciate that.
It does seem like this is a great program and and it would be wise to to continue in
this direction of trying to find more customers.
Mr. Chairman, you don't need to invoke me when you say that.
But thank you.
I've been with a long time already today.
You're well, I'm fully caffeinated.
Yeah, you look like.
All right.
Any questions on our two other questions?
All right. You've heard staff's recommendation on our two all in favor of approving the
recommendation. Say aye.
Aye.
Aye.
Any opposed?
All right. Our two passes unanimously moving on to our three.
Good morning. Benjamin Deutschman with the commission staff.
That's the second part of that similar issue.
It's docket number 56002 Georgia Power Company's 2025 integrated resource plan
and docket number 56003 Georgia Power Company's 2025 application for the certification,
decertification, and amended demand side management plan.
Georgia Power Company's application for approval of the 2026 plan hatch units one through two
nuclear extended power upgrades on September 21st, 2026, pursuant to the order adopting
stipulation in Georgia Power Company's 2025 integrated resource plan.
Georgia Power submitted to the commission this application.
The proposed plan will eventually add 49 megawatts of additional capacity at the existing plant
hatch nuclear units and leverages carbon free energy, customer subscriptions,
and benefits from the inflation reduction act for the benefit of all customers.
Staff recommends commission approve the plant hatch one and two nuclear project.
Y'all have just voted for the tariff.
All right. Thank you, Dr. Band. Any questions for the good doctor on our three?
No questions. I do want to just make a comment to explain why it is that I'll vote the way that
I'll vote. Mr. Deutschman, you actually hesitated for Commissioner Wise's question of whether or
not this new customer is fully paying for it. I think they're mostly fully paying for it,
but not 100%. And specifically, with this approval, we're going to be deferring depreciation
and interest expenses. And because of the rate freeze last year, that's a specific example of where
the company's bottom line will be improved until rates are reset.
But ultimately, I have looked at the backup. And I think that this is in the interests of
rate payers. I think there are benefits that are flowing here. And that is why
I think I'll be supportive of this. I do think, though, that one concern is that there isn't a
specific, and I'm not going to offer a motion to change this at the moment, but there is no
cost cap here. There is no rider to make sure that any cost overruns are assigned to the
customers that are incurring this. And that is a concern, I think, with the rate payer protection
pledge. But I still think, as constructed, this is worth supporting.
Any other questions on R3? All right. Thank you. All right. We'll move on. All in favor of approving
staff's recommendation on item R3, say aye. Aye. Any opposed? R3 passes unanimously.
All right. Was there any other matters to be taken up on the utility division agenda?
All right. We'll move on to administrative affairs, where we have a consent agenda.
Does any commissioner wish to hold any item or move it from consent to regular agenda?
All right. If not, all in favor of approving the administrative affairs consent agenda, say aye.
Any opposed? Administrative affairs consent agenda passes unanimously. Was there any other
business to be taken up today? All right. Well, thank you all again for being with us.
We are adjourned.
